title: Christopher Nolan's Odyssey Nears Hollywood's Top 6 All-Time in India
excerpt: At ₹189.9 crore after 52 days, the Nolan epic needs only a fraction more to pass Avatar: Fire And Ash's ₹190.5 crore and claim the No. 6 spot among Hollywood's biggest Indian grossers ever.
body:
Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey is one box-office weekend away from entering Hollywood's all-time top six in India. After 52 days in theaters, the epic fantasy stands at ₹188.14 crore net, having overtaken The Jungle Book (₹188 crore) to become the seventh highest-grossing Hollywood film ever on Indian screens — with Avatar: Fire And Ash's ₹190.5 crore now barely ₹2.4 crore ahead, according to Koimoi's tracking.

"Globally, the film has crossed $1.6 billion and become Universal Pictures' highest-grossing film of all time with $1.68 billion worldwide, per industry tracking."

The film's latest all-time tally of ₹189.9 crore (updated September 15) leaves it roughly ₹0.6 crore short of the No. 6 slot, a gap it has been closing steadily at around ₹1.7 crore per weekend in its eighth week. The day-52 Sunday alone pulled in ₹68 lakh, following ₹64 lakh on Saturday — remarkable endurance for a film in the final phase of its theatrical run.

Context & Background

The Odyssey opened to ₹85.65 crore in its first week and held up through word-of-mouth, collecting ₹45.67 crore in week two and ₹23.69 crore in week three despite losing screens to Spider-Man: Brand New Day. That rival has since become the first Hollywood film to cross ₹500 crore in India (₹500.21 crore and counting), which makes The Odyssey's own milestone more striking — it achieved its run while sharing the calendar with one of the biggest Hollywood releases India has ever seen.

Nolan's brand has carried the film far beyond its opening. The Odyssey is now the director's highest-grossing film in India, surpassing Oppenheimer's ₹129 crore, and it has survived eight weeks on sheer consistency — one of the most leggy Hollywood runs of recent years in the country.

Globally, the film has crossed $1.6 billion and become Universal Pictures' highest-grossing film of all time with $1.68 billion worldwide, per industry tracking. It also topped the South Korean box office for 40 consecutive days, per the Korea JoongAng Daily — evidence of the film's unusual stamina across very different Asian markets.

Impact & Analysis

The top-six threshold matters because it rewrites the all-time Hollywood hierarchy in India. Avatar: Fire And Ash itself entered the chart only last year at No. 6 with ₹190.5 crore. The Odyssey catching it in its ninth week would displace a film released barely a year ago — a fast turnover at the top of a list otherwise dominated by films released years apart, from Avatar: The Way of Water (₹390.6 crore) to Avengers: Endgame (₹373.22 crore).

The week-wise breakdown tells the story of a run built on retention rather than opening weekend fireworks: after a ₹85.65 crore start, the film declined gently through weeks two (₹45.67 crore), three (₹23.69 crore) and four (₹15.65 crore), then settled into long-tail earnings of ₹7.39, ₹5.57 and ₹2.82 crore across weeks five through seven. That pattern — a slow, audience-driven burn — is the opposite of the front-loaded blockbusters it now outranks.

Should it cross ₹190.5 crore this weekend, only Spider-Man: No Way Home (₹212 crore) stands between it and the top five. The eventual ceiling depends on how many more weeks exhibitors hold it — the film's eighth-weekend ₹1.7 crore suggests the screen life isn't over yet.

Diaspora Angle

This is Indian audiences shaping Hollywood history. The ₹189.9 crore India haul makes The Odyssey one of Nolan's defining global territories, and the diaspora's word-of-mouth — from North American screens to Indian family-group debates about the epic — has amplified a run that now ranks India among the film's most consequential markets. For NRI moviegoers, the India numbers add a second storyline to enjoy: the film isn't just a global hit, it's a hit where it counts most for their box-office bragging rights.

What's Next

The math is simple: another weekend at the current pace puts The Odyssey at roughly ₹190.6 crore, just past Avatar: Fire And Ash. Watch the Friday-through-Sunday figures — if the ninth weekend holds above ₹1.5 crore, Hollywood's top six in India gets a new member before the film's ninth week closes. The No. 5 spot (Spider-Man: No Way Home, ₹212 crore) remains a longer shot that would require an exceptional tenth week.
